title: Height and slope terrain splat material
purpose: Paint a three.js terrain mesh with sand, grass, rock and snow chosen per pixel from world height and slope, with smooth bands, noise-jittered boundaries and procedural colours, and an exact CPU mirror of the four weights. Use it for islands, mountains and procedural landscapes without splat maps.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE under WebGL 2 (unsigned integer GLSL and the colorspace_fragment chunk); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.name: createTerrainSplatMaterial
exports.summary: The terrain material; heights are world y; an unknown option throws TypeError.

exports.name: splatWeights
exports.signature: splatWeights(height, slope, settings = {}, noiseValue = 0.5) -> [sand, grass, rock, snow]
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the layer weights, which sum to 1; slope is 1 - normal.y.

exports.name: valueNoise2
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the GLSL 2D value noise in [0, 1).

exports.name: TERRAIN_SPLAT_GLSL
exports.summary: GLSL integer hash, valueNoise2 and splatWeights.

exports.name: TERRAIN_SPLAT_VERTEX
exports.summary: Vertex stage: world position and normal, InstancedMesh aware.

exports.name: TERRAIN_SPLAT_FRAGMENT
exports.summary: Fragment stage: weights, procedural layer colours and Lambert light.

options.name: sandLevel
options.meaning: Height where sand gives way to grass; below snowLevel.

options.name: band
options.meaning: Half width of each height transition.

options.name: rockSlope
options.meaning: Slope (1 - normal.y) where rock takes over.

options.name: slopeBand
options.meaning: Half width of the rock transition.

options.name: jitter
options.meaning: How far noise moves the height boundaries.

options.name: detail
options.meaning: Brightness variation of each layer from finer noise.

options.name: ambient
options.meaning: Share of the colour lit without the light.

limits: Procedural colours, not textured layers: there are no albedo, normal or roughness maps per layer, so close-ups look flat. Weights depend only on height, slope and noise, not on curvature, moisture, flow or painted masks. Heights are world y, so moving the mesh up or down moves the bands. The slope comes from vertex normals, so faceted or unsmoothed meshes paint in facets. Lit by one direction uniform; scene lights, shadows and fog are ignored. Requires WebGL 2 for unsigned integers in GLSL. Written for three.js r155 or later; only 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Height and slope layer weights with smoothstep bands
